AN ACT to authorize William J. Cooley and Patrick Humiston to receive certain

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1578

SPONSOR: GALLIVAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to authorize William J. Cooley and Patrick Humiston to receive
certain credit under section 384-d of the retirement and social security
law

 
PURPOSE OF THE BILL:

This legislation corrects a statutory deficiency by permitting Detective
William Cooley, of the Buffalo Police Department (BPD), the authority to
transfer service credit accrued resulting from his employment with the
Erie County Sheriff's Department to the pension plan of his existing
employer.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 establishes the authority to transfer service credit.

Section 2 requires past service costs to be borne by the City of
Buffalo.

Section 3 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

William Cooley and Patrick Humiston, due to circumstances beyond their
control were laid-off from their respective positions as sworn officers
with the Buffalo Police Department (BPD) in 2002, thereby requiring them
to seek alternative employment as Erie County Sheriff's Deputies for a
period of approximately three years. Messrs.  Cooley and Humiston were
subsequently reinstated to the BPD.

Given the aforementioned unique situation and their continued employment
as law enforcement officers, it is necessary to afford the option as set
forth within this legislation.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

See fiscal note.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The bill would take effect immediately.

summary: Authorizes William J. Cooley and Patrick Humiston, both currently city of Buffalo police officers, to receive certain credit under section 384-d of the retirement and social security law.
